title: Verify creating an application writes an audit log using direct SQLite
preconditions: The application is running and the job-tracker SQLite database is accessible
steps: 1. Send POST /api/v1/applications with a valid payload and status applied. 2. Save the returned application id. 3. Query application_audit_logs with sqlite3 for rows created within the last 3 minutes.
expected_result: The create response is 201. At least one matching recent audit-log row exists with action created, a populated user_id, and old_status set to null.

title: Verify creating an application writes an audit log using SQLClient
preconditions: The application is running and SQLClient can access the job-tracker database
steps: 1. Send POST /api/v1/applications with a valid payload and status applied. 2. Save the returned application id. 3. Query application_audit_logs with SQLClient for rows created within the last 3 minutes.
expected_result: The create response is 201. The query returns an audit-log row with action created, a populated user_id, and old_status set to null.

title: Verify a status update records previous and new statuses in the audit log
preconditions: The application is running and SQLClient can access the job-tracker database
steps: 1. Create an application through POST /api/v1/applications with status potential. 2. Send PATCH /api/v1/applications/{application_id} with status applied. 3. Query application_audit_logs with SQLClient for rows created within the last 2 minutes.
expected_result: An audit-log row for the status change records old_status as potential and new_status as applied.
